turns.assessment: O1 is onset-coincident and shows a large pre-FEC BER degradation confined to receiver trx.och47.z at S15. Its received power, estimated OSNR, DGD, SOP rate, the opposite endpoint, channel monitors, and intervening amplifiers showed no change, strongly indicating a receiver-local penalty rather than an optical-path fault. O2 occurred much later on an unrelated section and is not causal.

proposals.rationale: The receiver's pre-FEC BER changed at the service onset while all its other optical metrics and upstream path instrumentation remained stable—the documented signature of receiver-local degradation.
A channel-specific filter penalty can reduce quality without changing power, but stable receiver and path metrics make it less likely than a local receiver fault.
Margin erosion could increase BER without a power alarm, but it is normally gradual rather than the distinct onset seen near t=600 s.
